## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Functional interfaces
//
// Capabilities of function-like values: things that map a domain to a range.
// Curves, surfaces, fields, easings, and distributions are all procedural.
//
// The domain/range pair alone identifies the kind of object, which is why one
// interface covers so much ground. Named forward interfaces, by instantiation:
//   Number -> Number ......... ICurve1D, Easing        Number -> Point2D/3D ... ICurve2D/3D
//   UvCoordinate -> Point3D .. IParametricSurface      UvwCoordinate -> Point3D IParametricVolume
//   Point2D -> Number ........ IScalarField2D          Point3D -> Number ...... IScalarField3D
//     (zero level = a boundary: ISignedDistanceField2D/3D)
//   Point2D -> Point2D ....... IDeformation2D          Point3D -> Point3D ..... IDeformation3D
//     (read as displacement instead: IVectorField2D/3D)
//   Point2D -> Boolean ....... IImplicitRegion2D       Point3D -> Boolean ..... IImplicitVolume3D
//   Point2D/3D -> Color ...... IColorField2D/3D        Point2D -> Matrix2x2 ... ITensorField2D
// An integer domain makes the mapping a lattice read rather than a continuous
// one: that is a sampled image, texture, or voxel grid, not a field.

// A pure mapping from a domain value to a range value. The unifying interface for
// curves (Number to point), surfaces (UV to point), fields (point to value),
// easings (Number to Number), and beyond.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics))
interface IProcedural<TDomain, TRange>
{
    Eval(x: Self, input: TDomain): TRange;
}

// A procedural mapping that can be evaluated in reverse.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bijection)
interface IBijective<TDomain, TRange>
    inherits IProcedural<TDomain, TRange>
{
    EvalInverse(x: Self, output: TRange): TDomain;
}

// Repeats with a fixed period in its domain: Eval(t) equals Eval(t + Period).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodic_function)
// TPeriod is bounded so that phase arithmetic on the period is derivable:
// IModular supplies the remainder and IAdditive the correction that makes it
// land in [0, Period) for negative inputs (see WrapPhase in
// functional-procedural.library.plato).
interface IPeriodic<TPeriod>
    where TPeriod: IAdditive, TPeriod: IModular
{
    Period(x: Self): TPeriod;
}

// Has a preferred parameter domain over which evaluation is meaningful.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain_of_a_function)
interface IParameterDomain
{
    Domain(x: Self): NumberInterval;
}
```
